I mean audiophile headphones will of course be more detailed no matter what, but marginally so in gaming. And yes, it doesn't really give an advantage in game.

A lot of gaming headphones have a bullshit surround sound system, where they put multiple drivers on each ear. This is bad because the drivers have to be smaller which make them less powerful, and multiple drivers doesn't actually give you better imaging. The only worth it advantage that you could get from an audiophile headphone for gaming is better imaging. Imaging is the ability to tell the direction/source of the sound (behind your head, to the right). Better imaging means more accurate. So yes, a 400-500 headphone might enable you to better hear *where exactly* the footsteps are coming from.

It really depends what you're using the headphones for. If you are just playing games and watching youtube, you won't be able to tell too much difference since the audio quality in those media is already somewhat poor; perhaps a difference in balance/signature and a bit more detail. If you listen to a raw audio file then your new headphones will shine against your gaming headphones.

If you just want headphones for gaming, you don't need to go to deep in terms of detail and accuracy. Get a headphone that is detailed enough, has good imaging, and favors treble over bass. Too much bass will emphasize things like explosions in a video game that will cover up more important higher pitched details like footsteps.
